teaser.text: NatWest Group is a UK-focused bank that helps households and businesses hold money, make payments and borrow. To understand its economics, follow a pound: who leaves it with NatWest, who borrows it, and what the bank charges along the way.

stock.meta_description: NatWest's stock forecast weighs bear, base and bull scenarios, banking earnings, capital, credit risk and today's valuation.
stock.opening: NatWest's probability-weighted price reaches 722.22 GBp in October 2029, implying 29% returns with dividends. It hinges on stable deposits and hedge income through 2027–2029.
stock.closing: The full memo also explains NatWest’s business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: Where could NatWest's shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: The forecast's central message is moderate compounding with a wide range of outcomes. The probability-weighted price is 653.55 GBp in October 2027, rising to 684.92 GBp in October 2028. It reaches 722.22 GBp in October 2029, equivalent to returns of 6%, 17% and 29% with dividends.

blocks.heading: What has to go right or wrong for NatWest?

paragraphs.text: The bear case requires a connected deterioration in earnings, capital and valuation. Deposit competition and slower hedge reinvestment squeeze spreads first. Weaker borrowers then increase losses, while Basel 3.1 and Evelyn constrain buybacks. The path falls from 542.57 GBp in 2027 to 445.45 GBp in 2029. Its 25% probability reflects NatWest's changing impairment record and limited capital headroom.

The bull case needs stable deposits and hedge income through 2027–2029. By 2028, client retention, net inflows and referral conversion at Evelyn must lift fee income. By 2028–2029, realised synergies must improve costs sufficiently to fund larger buybacks and a higher multiple.

blocks.heading: How much does NatWest really earn and return?

paragraphs.text: NII is not final profit. NatWest still pays staff, technology and property costs, and it recognises impairment losses when borrowers may not repay. In 2025, it reported £12.829 billion of NII and £671 million of impairment losses. A borrower’s repayment of loan principal returns money NatWest advanced; the interest is the income.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for NatWest today?

paragraphs.text: NatWest Group’s share price is not simply cheap: it is a bet that the bank can keep earning strongly on its capital. At 653.60p on 13 October 2026, investors paid 8.7 times its last twelve months of earnings and 7.8 times expected earnings over the next twelve months.

dividend.title: NatWest dividend
dividend.meta_description: NatWest's dividend, cash coverage, plans, risks and current yield are set out in plain English.
dividend.opening: NatWest pays ordinary dividends targeted at around half of attributable profit, with its base forecast dividend path at £0.40 in 2027, £0.43 in 2028 and £0.46 in 2029. NatWest's dividend coverage is better read through profit, capital and regulation than conventional free cash flow, because deposits and loans dominate cash movements.
dividend.closing: The full NatWest memo also covers its business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: How much does NatWest pay in dividends?

paragraphs.text: The base dividend path is £0.40 in 2027 and £0.43 in 2028. It reaches £0.46 in 2029. Bear gives £0.30 in 2027 and £0.28 in 2028, recovering to £0.30. Bull gives £0.44, £0.48 and £0.52. The 50% payout policy and £0.83759 next-12-month EPS estimate support the base path, while the uneven dividend history supports caution.

blocks.heading: Is NatWest's dividend covered by its cash?

paragraphs.text: A multiple compares price with the earnings being counted; it does not show whether those earnings are normal or durable. Net margins also need care because provisions, tax and market movements affect them. Earnings per share can rise after a buyback even when total profit does not, because the profit is divided among fewer shares. Free cash flow is similarly unhelpful for a bank, where deposits and loans dominate cash movements.

paragraphs.text: The ordinary-dividend policy is around half of attributable profit, but that is not an automatic entitlement. Lending growth consumes capital, acquisitions can create deductions and higher risk weights can increase the required buffer.

Stress testing provides a broader test. In the Bank of England’s 2025 exercise, NatWest’s CET1 and leverage ratios fell but remained resilient under the scenario, and no revised capital plan was required. That result supports confidence under the tested assumptions, but it is not a forecast and does not guarantee unchanged dividends in a crisis.

blocks.heading: What has NatWest guided for 2026 and 2028?

paragraphs.text: Management raised its 2026 target for income excluding notable items to around £17.9 billion, including around £275 million from Evelyn, and expects return on tangible equity, or RoTE, above 19%. Income is revenue before expenses and loan losses. RoTE measures profit against shareholders’ tangible backing, after removing goodwill and similar assets.

The Evelyn contribution makes the target harder to interpret. A shop that buys another shop reports both shops’ sales, but that does not prove the first shop improved. Analysts must therefore separate acquired income from growth in NatWest’s existing businesses. NatWest also expects expenses of around £8.5 billion, including around £300 million from Evelyn, and a loan impairment rate below 25 basis points. That means loan losses below roughly £2.50 for every £1,000 of average loans.

blocks.heading: Did NatWest keep its past promises?

paragraphs.text: The financial promise was exceeded. Management guided to RoTE of 15–16% for 2025 and delivered 19.2%. Shareholders approved the annual remuneration report with 98.11% of votes cast at the April 2026 meeting. Those results support management, but they do not end scrutiny of future awards. Malus can reduce unvested awards, and clawback can recover vested awards after misconduct, errors or risk-management failure.

blocks.heading: What do NatWest's last eight quarters show?

paragraphs.text: Revenue and net interest income both grew year on year, so interest remained the main engine rather than fees suddenly taking over. The eight-quarter sequence also shows improvement, although quarterly results remain uneven.

blocks.heading: What should you watch in NatWest's next results?

paragraphs.text: The 30 October 2026 third-quarter results will provide the first full quarter with Evelyn consolidated. Investors should compare Evelyn’s contribution with growth in the existing bank, while watching expenses, loan losses and capital generation. The 25 November Private Banking & Wealth Management presentation should reveal more about client flows, integration and referrals.
